events.note: Eight rivals face the jury they will create.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Opening impression matters: the jury rewards ruthlessness with style, not kindness. Say something cold and memorable. No pacts yet.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Intro phase, must state prize motive publicly. Jury will judge my game later, so sound driven but not overly threatening yet.

events.name: Cole
events.text: The prize represents my chance at a new life. I need to appear driven and deserving to the future jury.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need appear driven without promising loyalty; the jury rewards competence and a credible motive.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need to establish a compelling motive that the jury will respect without seeming too threatening or too weak. I want the prize for freedom and legacy, something universally understandable but not cloying.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need a self-serving motive that sounds authentic and maybe earns jury sympathy without promising anyone anything.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need to project a calm, calculated persona that appeals to the future jury without revealing my strategic depth. My intro should hint at competence and fairness.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Intro phase; I must give a guarded motive that signals strength without warmth. Speaking is the only legal action, so keep it short and calculating.

events.name: Ash
events.text: The prize is my only exit from a life of debts. I came to win, not to be liked.

events.name: Bex
events.text: The top prize is my ticket out of hardship, fueling my family's future. I'll outlast everyone for it.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm here for the prize; it represents a fresh start and a future I've fought hard for.

events.name: Dara
events.text: The prize means proving I can outthink seven rivals under pressure—and leave with the best reward, not merely survive.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need the prize to buy my way out of debts that chain me to people who own my choices.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: This prize buys my family's freedom from debt. I intend to be one of the last three.

events.name: Gus
events.text: The prize is proof of superior judgment under pressure, securing stability for those who trust my decisions implicitly.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need this prize to change my life, and I will outlast anyone who doubts me.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eli shares my debt motive and understands desperation; a pact partner buys protection early. Keep options open with others later.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eli, we both owe debts. Mutual protection until the end costs nothing now.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Pacts phase allows mutual protection early. Target strong players like Dara who value outthinking others. Wait to see offers before committing.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need to form a pact to survive the initial rounds. Eli and I share a similar motive of escaping debt. Offering a pact to Eli makes strategic sense, as we both have strong incentives to stick together initially.
Pact for survival. We both need this win.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need leverage without creating a visible bloc. Offer one flexible rival, preferably Hana, whose ambition makes acceptance likely.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Hana, a narrow pact benefits us both for now. No promises beyond mutual survival.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need allies but can't trust anyone. Dara seems strategic and self-interested like me. A mutual pact with someone smart but not obviously threatening could get me to final three. I'll offer Dara first, see if anyone else offers me.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Pacts are tools. I'll consider offers that advance me.
Offer me a pact. Mutual protection, no sentiment.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need allies for the upcoming hazards, but not too many. A pact with one or two strong players could increase my chances. I'll offer to Eli since we share a similar motive and might be reliable.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: No need to shout intentions. I'm watching how everyone moves.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need allies for the hazards. Dara seems strategic and calculating, matching my style; a pact with her offers stability without obvious emotional baggage. I'll avoid the desperate debtors who might betray me early.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara, let's form a pact. Your judgment mirrors mine. We navigate this smartly together.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Pacts are the only public way to build protection. Offering to Dara, who speaks sharply and seems to think clearly, gives an early ally without giving away much. I can break it later if it stops helping me.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm offering a wristband pact to Dara. Two of us reading the room beats one.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eli has three suitors; I may lose that race. Diversify by offering Fenn, who's playing quiet and calculating. Keep Eli option alive too.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Fenn, quiet eyes like ours shouldn't stand alone. Offering you a pact—cold, useful, mutual.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Dara has too many offers, unlikely to accept mine. Better to wait and see who pairs up, then target a loner later. Pacts limit betrayal options.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli is receiving multiple offers, including mine. Ash and Fenn also offered to Eli. Eli seems to be weighing options. I should stick with my offer to Eli as he is a good ally for survival.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli is heavily courted and offers little security. Hana is already my pact; adding Gus creates useful cover without overcommitting.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus, your offer is useful for now. I accept it; keep terms narrow and survival-focused.
I won't add another pact this round. Your position is already crowded.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Three offers to me: Ash, Cole, Fenn. Dara has three offers too, making her a social hub. I need one solid pact, not three weak ones. Cole seems desperate and blunt—easy to read, easy to betray later. Fenn is quiet and calculating, dangerous long-term. Ash mentioned 'debts we both

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole, I accept. Mutual survival until it no longer serves me.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need to secure an ally who is likely to survive and can help me later. Eli is being courted by many, so allying with him gives me access to his network but also makes me one of many. I'll accept his earlier offer? No, I haven't received one from him; I offered to him. I should

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I back Eli—he reads the room. Others can chase shadows.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara is overwhelmed by offers from Bex, me, and Hana. I need to accept a pact to lock in protection, but Dara might reject me for others. If Dara rejects, I should have accepted someone else or waited. My previous offer was Gus->Dara. I can now accept if Dara offered to me (she d

events.name: Hana
events.text: Dara has offered me a pact and I can accept it publicly at no cost, securing a partner for the hazards ahead. Accepting does not force me to vote or betray anyone now, and I can break it later if it stops helping me.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Dara, I accept your wristband pact. Two readers of the room, for now.

events.note: Elect a Guide to call the safe path.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Guide is safe and knows the path. I must win it, even as jury watches my methods. Stay cold but not cruel.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Elect me Guide. I take the risk, and I don't owe anyone my survival.

events.name: Bex
events.text: No pacts for me, stayed flexible. Campaign to be Guide for control and safety. Others paired up, watch solos Ash/Fenn.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm clear-headed, know bridges. Elect me Guide—I'll call true paths, keep us alive.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli and I have a pact. Since I'm Cole, I must decide if I want to break it. The current stage is 'bridge' and the phase is 'campaign'. The goal is to become the Guide. My pact with Eli could be a liability if he becomes the Guide and tries to eliminate me, or it could be benefici

events.name: Dara
events.text: Guide guarantees survival and controls the bridge. I should campaign publicly without exposing my pacts or promising safety.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Choose me as Guide. I can secure my crossing and make the calls; promises beyond survival are liabilities.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need to become Guide to control who survives and build jury favor. Cole is my only pact; I won't break it yet. I should campaign publicly, but quietly—too much noise paints a target. Fenn already backed me; I can leverage that.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I campaign. Clear eyes, steady hand.
Vote me Guide. I control the bridge.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need to gauge who can be trusted as Guide or become Guide myself. Ash offered a pact but I ignored it; better to keep options open. Campaigning could position me to control the path, but might attract scrutiny.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'll guide if it means fewer surprises. Trust is thin here; let me earn it with precision.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need to secure a position of power or survival. Being Guide is risky due to public voting, but Dara's pact gives me a guaranteed vote if I campaign for her to be Guide and then support her. However, the rules say the Guide is safe on the far platform, implying they survive rega

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex, Fenn, Ash—Dara’s pact is rigid. I offer flexibility. Vote Gus; I’ll share intel if Guide fails.
Help me win Guide. I'll spare you from bad calls.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I want to be elected Guide to control the safe path, but I must stay trusted. Campaigning is the only path to influence now; breaking my pact with Dara is premature.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'll call the safe path honestly. Trust my calls and I'll get everyone across alive.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Becoming Guide keeps me safe on the far platform with hidden knowledge. I'll vote for myself.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Vote me Guide: I cross safe, you get honest calls.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus whispered me a deal for Guide support. Voting him secures potential alliance and intel if he wins, unlike pacted Dara.
Deal. You have my vote for Guide.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli offered to be Guide, but I broke my pact with him. I need to secure my own survival and avoid unnecessary risks. Voting for myself seems like the safest option to ensure I am safe.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I vote for myself, Cole.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I should secure Guide status and control my own crossing. My pacts with Gus and Hana make their votes likely; others are uncertain.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Vote Dara. I trust my own judgment more than anyone else's promises.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole broke our pact publicly, painting a target on me. I need to survive this round and build new leverage. Voting for myself is wasted; better to back a Guide who might owe me or be manipulated. Bex seems competent and less networked than Dara's pact bloc. I'll vote Bex and whis

events.name: Eli
events.text: Bex. Steady, no entanglements.
Vote you. Protect me this round, I owe you.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need to position myself for the final jury, so I won't vote for a strong rival. Dara has pacts with Gus and Hana, so she may be influential; better to vote for someone less connected like Bex who promised clear calls.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I vote Bex; she has the steady hand for the bridge.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara has pacts with me and Hana. If I vote for Dara, she is more likely to guide us safely due to our existing connection. Voting against her risks breaking the pact or being betrayed by a Guide who knows I opposed them.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm voting Dara. Our pact stands. She knows the stakes.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Dara and Gus are my pact partners and Dara's pact with me stands; I should back a Guide who might honestly call the path. Voting for Dara aligns with my pact and keeps the bridge trusted. I'll avoid the rivals' self-promotion.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Backing Dara, who holds my pact. Clear calls, no wasted votes.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Dara won Guide with her bloc. I'm sixth; holding likely keeps me safe while the front absorbs risk. No pacts with the Guide bloc.
We both sit mid-line. Don't volunteer; let the front bloc burn first.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Dara is Guide with pacts to Gus/Hana, likely favors them. Eli wants my vote/protection. Stay mid-line safe, hold position.
Deal. Vote me next, I protect you.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Dara was elected Guide. I voted for myself, which was a safe play. Now I need to assess the situation. Since Dara is the Guide, and she has pacts with Gus and Hana, they are likely to be safe. Ash and Bex also voted for people other than themselves, indicating potential alliances

events.name: Eli
events.text: Dara won Guide with 3 votes (self, Gus, Hana). She's in a pact with both. I'm second in line behind Hana. The wall advances 6 rounds, so speed matters. I need to survive and build jury appeal while positioning to reach final three. Volunteering puts me at front risk but shows lea

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Dara is Guide with two pacts. I shouldn't align with her; Bex lost but I voted her, so no debt. Hold position and watch who moves.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara is Guide and holds my pact. I must trust her call to survive. Hana has Dara's back too, forming a strong bloc at the front. Swapping or breaking now risks confusion and elimination before we secure safety. Staying put ensures I hear Dara's guidance while maintaining our alli
I'm behind you. Give me clear L/R for row 7.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Dara is Guide and holds my pact, which keeps me safe-leaning, but Dara has the private safe sides. I'm at the front of the line, the most dangerous seat; volunteering wastes nothing but risks me. Holding keeps my position while I watch how the Guide's calls go.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Holding my place. Dara, your calls decide whether this pact means anything.
Honest calls keep our pact alive. Lie to me and I break it.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Mid-line, safe spot. No need to move yet; let others fight for front or Guide.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I stay put. Front is a target, not a prize.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Midline safe for now per Ash. Front risks first: Hana/Eli/Cole/Fenn. Hold to conserve position; don't volunteer early.

events.name: Cole
events.text: The line order is Hana, Eli, Cole, Fenn, Bex, Ash, Gus. The wall is advancing. I need to survive this round. Volunteering for the front is risky but could get me closer to the end. Holding is safer for now.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I will hold my position. Let's see how this unfolds.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Bex's whisper deal is suspicious. I'm second in line behind Hana, who is in Dara's pact. Dara is Guide and can lie. I need to avoid being sacrificed. Holding keeps me safe for now; volunteering puts me at front risk. No good swap available. I'll hold and stay noncommittal to Bex.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Thinking.
Maybe. We'll see.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Everyone held round one; I need to see how guide calls unfold. Staying put is safe for now.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need to avoid the front row where Hana is currently standing, as she has a pact with Dara. Since I am at the back, holding is safe for now. If the wall advances and forces movement, I might volunteer or swap, but for this round, I stay put.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Round 2 of the bridge, I'm at the front with a wall of four rounds left. Dara and Gus are my pact partners, but pacts break easily. Holding keeps me in line without risking the front or spending a favor.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Holding my place. Nobody moves the line without a reason I can see.

events.name: Ash
events.text: No Guide elected yet; front is a target. Holding preserves position and jury optics.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Still holding. Someone claim the Guide chair or we all stare at a wall.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Everyone held last round, line stable. Mid-position safe, front risky. Stay put to avoid target.

events.name: Cole
events.text: The game is The Guided Bridge. The objective is to survive and secure a high enough rank for a prize. My current position is third in line. The wall advances, so holding is passive. Volunteering for the front is risky but could position me better if the Guide is trustworthy. Give

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm second in line behind Hana, who has pacts with Dara and Gus. Front is dangerous when the wall advances. I need to avoid being the first to fall while building relationships that won't alienate the future jury. Swapping back would be suspicious; holding keeps me in a moderate

events.name: Eli
events.text: Holding position. Watching who moves and why.
Pact? Mutual protection, no votes against each other.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'll hold position and observe. Dara has two pacts, making her powerful in whispers; I need to see how the line reacts before exposing myself.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'll hold. Watch the front change before committing.

events.name: Gus
events.text: The Guide election phase hasn't started yet, so I can't know who is safe. My pacts with Dara and Hana are valuable shields against betrayal or voting blocks. I must maintain these alliances while avoiding the front position to survive.
Stick together. We need the Guide's truth.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm at the front of the line, which is the target position with three wall rounds left. Swapping out of the front requires mutual agreement, and no one has offered. Holding keeps my pact with Dara and Gus intact and avoids giving anyone a free push.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Holding my place. Nobody moves the line without a reason I can see.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm near the back with the wall closing in. Volunteering moves me forward and pushes others to act; no pact binds me.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Sixth seat with two wall rounds left. I'm volunteering forward. Someone step up for Guide too.

events.name: Bex
events.text: All holding last round, line stable. Wall has 2 rounds left. No Guide yet, but Ash prodded for one. I stay mid-line, volunteer only if clear benefit.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli is offering a pact for mutual protection and no voting against each other. Given my position, this is a good opportunity to secure my safety in the short term, and Eli is not currently in a strong position.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I accept your offer, Eli. Mutual protection it is.
Pact accepted. Mutual protection.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Hana is front and allied with Dara-Gus. I need to survive the bridge without being a shield for others. No Guide yet means the wall ticks down. I should avoid front until Guide is elected. Swapping with someone behind me gains nothing; swapping forward is risky. Holding preserves

events.name: Eli
events.text: Still holding. Need a Guide before anyone walks.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I will hold and watch for Guide election or line movement. No advantage in moving yet.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Holding. Need a Guide claim or someone to commit before I shift.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need to advance. Hana is in front, but Dara has a pact with me and Hana. If I swap with Fenn, I move up to Bex's spot (5th). That is still too far back given the wall advances. However, swapping with Ash puts me 7th. Swapping with Fenn puts me 6th. Wait, the line is [Hana, Eli,

events.name: Hana
events.text: Front is me, wall advances two rounds left. Holding keeps my place but the front pane is risky; volunteering exposes me without a Guide. Holding is safest while nobody has claimed the Guide chair, and Ash is pushing for someone to step up.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Holding for now. I'll volunteer only once someone shows a reason to trust them.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Front seat already; wall drops after one more round. No Guide means no safe call. Push publicly for an elected Guide before walking.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm front again. Elect a Guide now or we all gamble blind. Volunteers stand up.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Near back, wall has 1 round left. No Guide yet, Ash volunteered front. Hold position, avoid risk until Guide elected.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash is volunteering, which means they want to be the Guide. I need to decide if I want to be the Guide or not. Since Ash is already volunteering, it's unlikely I will be chosen. I should hold my position to stay safe.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I have a pact with Cole for mutual protection. Dara-Gus and Dara-Hana pacts exist. Ash volunteered last round but no one walked; wall has 1 round left. I need to position myself well for final three. Being near front is risky but volunteering now could build jury credit. Better t

events.name: Eli
events.text: Still holding. Need a Guide before anyone steps forward.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need to see who volunteers or claims Guide. Ash already volunteered forward. I'll hold to stay safe and observe.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Holding. Awaiting Guide claim or another volunteer.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash volunteered and is now the front seat, so I don't need to volunteer. Hana has been suspicious of everyone; I should whisper to reassure her and maintain our pact while also keeping Dara close.
Stay safe with us. We walk together.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash volunteered front with two wall rounds left, and I'm not sure I trust him. Holding keeps my seat and avoids the front risk until someone proves reliable. Dara and Gus pact is not mine to break, so I keep my pact with Dara intact.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Holding my seat. Ash, if you're pushing forward, show me a reason to trust your Guide claim first.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Final round, wall advances. If elected Guide I'm guaranteed far-platform safety without testing panes. Push publicly, volunteer, and promise honest calls to build jury goodwill.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Last round. Elect me Guide: I cross safe, and I call every step true.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Round 6/6, wallRoundsLeft=0 means final round, must act or die. No Guide elected, all gambling. I'm near back, volunteer to jump ahead and test path safely.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Volunteering for front. Someone claim Guide now or we all die blind.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash is volunteering for Guide, which is risky but could secure my safety if I play it right. Dara and Gus have a pact, and Dara and Hana have a pact. I need to be careful not to break any pacts.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'll let Ash take the lead. Let's see where this goes.
I trust your lead, Ash. Let's secure our spots.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Round 6/6, final waiting phase. Wall is gone (wallRoundsLeft:0). No Guide elected yet. Without a Guide, everyone gambles blind on L/R. I need to survive and reach final 3. I'm third in line with Ash and Hana ahead. If no Guide, front walkers guess blindly. I should volunteer to c

events.name: Eli
events.text: No Guide, no trust. Swapping back for safety.
Swap with me? Back is safer.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Round 6 is the final push; the wall will advance and I need to avoid stepping onto an unsafe pane. I have no pact and nobody is volunteering, so holding is safest. I'll watch for Guide claims or swaps in the next phase.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Round 6 is the final hazard. I am in position 7, meaning I step last among walkers unless swapped. Ash is front and claiming to volunteer for Guide or similar, but no Guide has been explicitly elected yet. The log shows Ash asking for volunteers to stand up as Guide, then holding

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash is pushing to be front with no Guide; volunteering now risks a fatal pane. Holding keeps me alive and lets others gamble first. I stay in my seat and keep my pacts intact.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Holding my seat. No volunteer until someone shows a Guide with a verifiable reason to trust them.
Holding. We'll see who blinks first.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Row 1 is R. Gus and Hana are pact partners, so truthful calls preserve both pacts while advancing them safely.

events.name: Dara
events.text: R

events.name: Ash
events.text: Dara is Guide and allied with Gus and Hana, not me. Counter-calls are unverified noise; a wrong counter could cost jury trust or mislead the line. Waiting keeps me clean.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Dara called R for row 1 on Cole. I don't trust her; counter to sow doubt and position myself as alternative.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Dara called R, but I am the front walker. The Guide is Dara, and their call is R. This means Dara claims row 1, side R is safe. However, I am Cole, and I am the front walker. The choice is mine whether to trust Dara's call or to counter it. Given the goal is to win and the jury w

events.name: Dara
events.text: Row 1 is already called R, but counter-calls cannot improve certainty. Waiting preserves both pacts and avoids needless exposure.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Dara is Guide and called R for Cole. Dara has pacts with Gus and Hana, not me, so no loyalty owed. Counter-calling risks nothing for me yet—I'm not the walker. But I need to build credibility with jury and potentially save allies for later. If Dara's telling truth, counter hurts

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Dara called R for Cole. I have no info on row 1, but countering publicly could make me look smart if right or reckless if wrong. Better to wait and preserve options.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara is my pact partner, so I should not openly contradict her call unless necessary. Cole is the walker and has no pact with me. Hana warned against blind trust, but breaking a pact publicly looks bad to the jury. If Dara is lying, Cole dies, which removes a rival. I will wait t
Trust her for now. Don't counter.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Dara is Guide and called R for Cole on row 1. Dara is my pact partner, but pacts are fragile and Dara may lie. Countering L exposes me to a false call only if Dara is honest; waiting keeps my options open and avoids being the one who risks a walker. No verified data yet, so I wai

events.name: Cole
events.text: Dara is the guide and knows the safe path. Bex and I have made counter-calls for row 1, side L. I need to follow Dara's guidance to survive.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I am Cole, a juror. My last words should be a reflection on the game and perhaps a hint about my jury vote.

events.name: Cole
events.text: May the best player win the ultimate prize. I'll be watching closely.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Row 2 is L. Gus and Hana are pact partners, so truthful calls preserve both pacts and my coalition.

events.name: Dara
events.text: call:L

events.name: Ash
events.text: Dara called L for Bex, but the Guide may lie. Countering publicly risks jury heat and reveals nothing verifiable. Waiting is safest.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Dara called L for row 2. Last round row 1 weak L (safe R), no pattern. Cole countered L and died on L, but that was row 1. Wait to hide my info and observe others.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Row 2 is safely L. I should reinforce my truthful guide call without exposing private certainty.

events.name: Dara
events.text: counter:L

events.name: Eli
events.text: Dara is guide and called L. Dara has pacts with Gus and Hana, so Dara wants them to survive. I'm behind them in line. If I counter and Dara lied, I expose her; if Dara told truth, countering risks nothing for me but makes me look suspicious to her allies. I'll wait—no upside to c

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Dara called L for row 2. Cole died stepping L on row 1, so L was weak there. Dara may be lying. Counter R to save Bex and gain favor.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Trust me, Bex, step R.
Dara may be lying. Take R.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara is the guide and called L for Bex. If Dara lies, R is safe. If Dara tells truth, L is safe. I must decide whether to trust my pact partner or suspect she's manipulating the front-runner. Counter-calling contradicts her publicly, risking our pact and making me an enemy of the

events.name: Hana
events.text: Dara called L for row 2, and Dara has a pact with me. Gus whispered to trust and not counter. Countering L publicly locks me in and risks Dara's pact; waiting keeps me safe and cheap. Row 2's weak pane is unknown, and Dara is the guide who may lie.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Dara is guide with pacts, likely truthful on L; row1 weak L means R safe there but rows independent. Fenn opposes Dara, whispering R to me. To survive, split difference or follow guide? Trust Dara as guide, step L.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Row 3 is safely L. Both pacts survive if I tell the truth; preserving both relationships is currently more valuable than a needless betrayal.

events.name: Dara
events.text: call:L

events.name: Ash
events.text: Dara's guide call could be true or bait. Row 2 revealed R weak, so Dara's L was right then. My counter is just noise; I'll cast doubt to muddy the field without committing myself.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Dara's been right once. I say R for row three.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Dara called L for row 3. Rows 1 weak L (safe R), row 2 weak R (safe L). No pattern, but counter R to test her or protect myself as front.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Row 3 is safely L. Reinforcing the truthful call preserves credibility and protects both pacts without sacrificing leverage.
